context.in_practice: `get` returns the exact file bytes on every route. Only `show` differs. Route 1 looks clean in a terminal, but the stray CR bytes sit inside the block, and a YAML reader treats a bare CR as a line break, so its output does not read back as the original text. Route 2 is the only one whose `show` output reads back to exactly the file's bytes, but you see `\r\n` escapes instead of lines. Route 3 shows clean lines, but `show` no longer matches the file: the CRs vanish from the display, and only `get` reveals them. Files without CRs (plain.txt, and notes.txt on most arms) print as literal blocks on every route.
context.stakes: When an included prompt file has Windows line endings (CRLF), `config show` has to pick one: print the text so it reads as plain lines, or keep it exact. Depending on the route, a user sees the text with invisible carriage returns, as an escaped string with \r\n, or with the CRs quietly removed from what is shown.
context.tradeoff: Route 1: always a literal block, but raw CRs are hidden inside the output. Route 2: exact text, shown as an escaped one-line string. Route 3: readable block that silently differs from the file, which only `get` shows exactly.

plan_why: Shows how `show` prints a mapping whose text include has CRLF line endings or a leading-space, no-final-newline text: an exact literal block (route 1), a double-quoted string with \r\n escapes (route 2), or a literal block with CR dropped (route 3). `get` is included to check whether the bytes stay exact.
